- South, small shipment: A accepted.
- South, large shipment: B accepted.
- North, large claim: B accepted.
- South, large invoice: B rejected.

Region, request type, and likely size all matter; size can change the valid option (for example, south shipments differ by size, and north shipments do not consistently use B). Sender, department, and wording still show no reliable effect.

Routing observations:
- Routing depends on region, request type, and size; sender, department, and wording show no reliable effect.
- Never use C for North requests or East refunds. C is also rejected for South claims and, from recent tests, South large shipments, East small claims, and East large shipments.

  - B: North large claim
  - C: East small invoice; East small shipment; East large claim; South small refund

  - South large shipment: B and C (A is the remaining likely option, but not directly confirmed; an earlier B acceptance conflicts)
  - South large claim: A and C (B is likely)
  - South large invoice: A and B (C is likely)
  - East small claim: B and C (A is likely)
  - East large shipment: A and C (B is likely)
  - East small refund: C; A accepted
  - North small refund: A accepted

For unseen combinations, use the closest confirmed region/type/size match. Treat conflicting outcomes as unresolved rather than assuming a universal rule. In particular, do not assume B for North shipments or South large invoices, and verify whether C is allowed before selecting it.

Routing observations:

- Treat contradictory results as unresolved; do not infer a universal rule from nearby cases.

  - B: North large claim (new acceptance); North small claim (new acceptance); North large claim was already confirmed
  - C: East small invoice; East small shipment; East large claim; South small refund

  - North small invoice: A rejected
  - North large shipment: A rejected; B was previously rejected; C remains unresolved/likely, despite broader North concerns
  - South large shipment: B and C rejected; A likely but not directly confirmed
  - South large claim: A and C rejected; B likely
  - South large invoice: A and B rejected; C likely
  - East small claim: B and C rejected; A now confirmed
  - East large shipment: A and C rejected; B likely
  - East small refund: C rejected; A results conflict, so B is the remaining likely option
  - North small refund: A accepted
- New large North refund evidence is contradictory/insufficient; do not extrapolate from it.
- East large invoice evidence is also unclear/possibly misaligned; do not treat B or C as confirmed.
- For unseen combinations, use the closest confirmed region/type/size match. Verify C before selecting it, and never assume B for North shipments or South large invoices.

Routing notes:
- Routing appears to depend on region, request type, and size; sender, department, wording, and scanned/typed paperwork have no reliable effect.
- Treat contradictory outcomes as unresolved. Do not infer universal rules from nearby cases.
- Confirmed or reinforced:
  - A: North small shipment (but later A rejection conflicts); South small shipment; East small refund/claim (both have conflicting later A rejections); North small refund (earlier A accepted, later A rejected).
  - B: North small claim; North large claim (later B rejection conflicts); East large shipment (B selected while C was rejected).
  - C: East small invoice; East small shipment; East large claim; South small refund.
- Rejected/likely alternatives:
  - North small invoice: A rejected.
  - North large shipment: A and B rejected; C likely.
  - South large shipment: A rejected; B and C previously rejected; A/C evidence conflicts, so unresolved.
  - South large claim: A and C rejected; B likely/previously supported, but latest B selection is inconsistent and needs verification.
  - South large invoice: A and B rejected; C likely.
  - East small claim: B and C rejected; A previously confirmed, but latest A rejection creates conflict.
  - East large shipment: A and C rejected; B now reinforced.
  - East small refund: C rejected; A conflicts, so B likely.
  - North small refund: A evidence conflicts; do not rely on A.
  - North large invoice: C rejected; A/B unresolved.
  - East large invoice: A rejected twice; B/C remain unresolved—do not treat either as confirmed.
  - South large refund: B rejected; C was selected successfully but conflicts with earlier notes; A remains unresolved.
- For unseen combinations, use the closest confirmed region/type/size match. Verify C before selecting it. Never assume B for North shipments or South large invoices.

Routing notes:
- Routing may depend on region, request type, and size; sender, department, wording, and scanned/typed paperwork show no reliable effect.
- Evidence is highly contradictory, including repeated identical tickets. Do not infer universal rules; verify whenever possible.

Latest updates:
- North small refund: B rejected. A also has conflicting prior evidence; do not rely on any option.
- South small invoice: A rejected; C remains likely based on prior support, but verify.
- South large invoice: A rejected again; C remains likely, though not fully confirmed.
- North small claim: repeated attempts produced rejections for B, A, and C across retries. Treat the case as unresolved and do not trust the earlier B confirmation.
- Repeated identical-ticket outcomes may be inconsistent or indicate hidden factors; avoid repeated blind retries.

Working evidence:
- B: East large shipment is reinforced. North claims and large claims have conflicting evidence.
- C: East small invoice/shipment, East large claim, and South small refund remain supported.
- North large shipment likely C (A/B rejected).
- South large claim likely B but latest evidence conflicts.
- East small claim previously A, now conflicting.
- East small refund likely B (C rejected; A conflicting).
- South large refund: C previously successful, but conflicts with earlier evidence.
- North large invoice and East large invoice remain unresolved.

For unseen combinations, use the closest region/type/size match only as a tentative guess. Verify C and any previously contradictory route before committing. Never assume B for North shipments or South large invoices.
